name: endlessh
desc: SSH tarpit that slowly sends an endless banner
why: An SSH tarpit that drips an endless banner to trap bots, a delightful door into how SSH banners and connection handling actually work.

brief.what_it_is: Endlessh is a small standalone C program that acts as an SSH tarpit. It listens on a port and, for each connecting client, slowly sends an endless stream of random SSH banner lines, one line every few seconds by default, so the client stays stuck. Its input is incoming TCP connections on the listening port, and its output is the drip of banner lines plus optional log messages to stdout or syslog. It is meant to sit on the port that bots probe while the real SSH server moves elsewhere.
brief.why_it_exists: The author's aim is to move the real SSH server to another port and let script kiddies get stuck in the tarpit instead of bothering a real server. The README says it keeps SSH clients locked up for hours or even days at a time.
brief.how_it_works: The tarpit works inside the banner phase, before any cryptographic exchange, so the program needs no crypto libraries. It is a single-threaded C program that uses poll() to hold many clients at once. Each line is randomized in length up to a configurable maximum, and lines are sent with a configurable millisecond delay.

commands_seen.context: Runs the daemon with basic logging, sending stdout to endlessh.log and stderr to endlessh.err.
Build override for RHEL 6 / CentOS 6, where clock_gettime is still in librt.
Build override for Solaris / illumos to link the extra libraries those systems need.
Solaris build example for a non-GCC/Clang compiler, clearing GCC-specific flags.

brief.install_notes: Beyond brew install, the README describes no required hardware, accounts or runtimes. The default config path is /etc/endlessh/config, loaded only if -f is given. Argument order matters, since options after -f override the config file. The default listening port is 2222, so the real SSH server must be moved elsewhere first. Building from source is done with make. Special build flags are needed only on old glibc, Solaris/illumos, and OpenBSD, where the man page install path differs.
brief.standout: It needs no cryptography and no threads: it wins by stalling clients in the banner stage with a poll() loop. The README's own sample config reads like OpenSSH config, and SIGHUP reloads it without a restart.
brief.status: unknown. The README gives no release date, changelog or last-commit information, and I did not follow the releases or commits pages. The scout notes say nothing about upkeep either.
brief.caveats: It is a defensive tool that the operator must place on the port that scanners hit, so the real SSH server has to be moved, and the README does not explain how to do that. Build notes cover only specific old or unusual systems. The README does not mention a license, so I could not confirm terms from the page I read. By default it logs nothing, and -v must be given to see activity.
quotes: Endlessh is an SSH tarpit that very slowly sends an endless, random SSH banner.
It keeps SSH clients locked up for hours or even days at a time.
The purpose is to put your real SSH server on another port and then let the script kiddies get stuck in this tarpit instead of bothering a real server.
